ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

1	package store
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"strconv"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
10	)
11	
12	// SetApproval records who approved which revision, while the campaign is
13	// still in review at version. It reports false when the campaign moved on.
14	// It runs before the in_review -> approved transition, because the CHECK on
15	// campaigns wants an approved campaign to name its approved revision.
16	func SetApproval(ctx context.Context, db DB, id, revisionID, by string, version int) (bool, error) {
17		tag, err := db.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE campaigns SET approved_revision_id = $2, approved_by = $3, approved_at = now(), updated_at = now()
18			WHERE id = $1 AND state = 'in_review' AND version = $4`, id, revisionID, by, version)
19		return tag.RowsAffected() == 1, err
20	}
21	
22	// LockCampaign reads a campaign and locks its row for the transaction.
23	func LockCampaign(ctx context.Context, db DB, id string) (Campaign, error) {
24		return scanCampaign(db.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT `+campaignCols+` FROM campaigns WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE`, id))
25	}
26	
27	// InsertMessagesFrom inserts one queued message per user id that
28	// audienceSQL selects, skipping any that already exist, and returns the new
29	// message ids. audienceSQL comes from segment.AudienceQuery (consent
30	// included) with its args as $1..$n.
31	func InsertMessagesFrom(ctx context.Context, db DB, campaignID, revisionID, channel, audienceSQL string, args []any) ([]string, error) {
32		n := len(args)
33		sql := `INSERT INTO messages (campaign_id, revision_id, user_id, channel)
34			SELECT $` + strconv.Itoa(n+1) + `, $` + strconv.Itoa(n+2) + `, a.id, $` + strconv.Itoa(n+3) + `
35			FROM (` + audienceSQL + `) a
36			ON CONFLICT (campaign_id, user_id, channel) DO NOTHING RETURNING id::text`
37		rows, err := db.Query(ctx, sql, append(append([]any{}, args...), campaignID, revisionID, channel)...)
38		if err != nil {
39			return nil, err
40		}
41		return pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowTo[string])
42	}
43	
44	// CountMessages counts a campaign's messages.
45	func CountMessages(ctx context.Context, db DB, campaignID string) (int, error) {
46		var n int
47		err := db.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM messages WHERE campaign_id = $1`, campaignID).Scan(&n)
48		return n, err
49	}
50	
51	// Outcome is what a campaign's messages add up to.
52	type Outcome struct {
53		Unfinished int // queued or sending
54		Failures   int // failed or dead
55	}
56	
57	// MessageOutcome counts a campaign's unfinished and failed messages.
58	func MessageOutcome(ctx context.Context, db DB, campaignID string) (Outcome, error) {
59		var o Outcome
60		err := db.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE state IN ('queued', 'sending')),
61				count(*) FILTER (WHERE state IN ('failed', 'dead'))
62			FROM messages WHERE campaign_id = $1`, campaignID).Scan(&o.Unfinished, &o.Failures)
63		return o, err
64	}
65	
66	// Send is everything the send worker needs about one message: its state,
67	// its campaign, its copy and its recipient. Contact fields go to the
68	// provider only; they are never logged.
69	type Send struct {
70		ID, CampaignID, Channel, State string
71		Attempts                       int
72		FirstAttemptAt                 *time.Time
73		CampaignState                  string
74		CampaignURL                    string
75		SMSBody, EmailSubject          string
76		EmailBody                      string
77		FirstName, LastName, City      string
78		Phone, Email                   string
79		Consent                        bool // for this message's channel
80	}
81	
82	// LoadSend reads a message with its campaign, revision and recipient, or
83	// returns ErrNotFound.
84	func LoadSend(ctx context.Context, db DB, id string) (Send, error) {
85		var s Send
86		err := db.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT m.id::text, m.campaign_id::text, m.channel::text, m.state::text, m.attempts, m.first_attempt_at,
87				c.state::text, coalesce(c.campaign_url, ''), r.sms_body, r.email_subject, r.email_body,
88				u.first_name, u.last_name, u.city, u.phone, u.email,
89				CASE m.channel WHEN 'sms' THEN u.consent_sms ELSE u.consent_email END
90			FROM messages m
91			JOIN campaigns c ON c.id = m.campaign_id
92			JOIN campaign_revisions r ON r.id = m.revision_id
93			JOIN users u ON u.id = m.user_id
94			WHERE m.id = $1`, id).Scan(&s.ID, &s.CampaignID, &s.Channel, &s.State, &s.Attempts, &s.FirstAttemptAt,
95			&s.CampaignState, &s.CampaignURL, &s.SMSBody, &s.EmailSubject, &s.EmailBody,
96			&s.FirstName, &s.LastName, &s.City, &s.Phone, &s.Email, &s.Consent)
97		if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
98			return Send{}, ErrNotFound
99		}
100		return s, err
101	}
102	
103	// Every message update below is guarded by the states it may come from, so
104	// a late or duplicate run cannot move a message backwards. Each reports
105	// whether it applied.
106	
107	func applied(tag interface{ RowsAffected() int64 }, err error) (bool, error) {
108		return err == nil && tag.RowsAffected() == 1, err
109	}
110	
111	// SkipMessage marks a queued (or reclaimed sending) message skipped.
112	func SkipMessage(ctx context.Context, db DB, id, class string) (bool, error) {
113		return applied(db.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE messages SET state = 'skipped', last_error_class = $2, next_attempt_at = NULL, updated_at = now()
114			WHERE id = $1 AND state IN ('queued', 'sending')`, id, class))
115	}
116	
117	// ClaimMessage moves a message to sending for one attempt and counts it. A
118	// message in sending may be claimed again: its last run crashed. It returns
119	// the attempt number and the first attempt time, or ok false.
120	func ClaimMessage(ctx context.Context, db DB, id string, now time.Time) (attempts int, first time.Time, ok bool, err error) {
121		err = db.QueryRow(ctx, `UPDATE messages SET state = 'sending', attempts = attempts + 1,
122				first_attempt_at = coalesce(first_attempt_at, $2), next_attempt_at = NULL, updated_at = now()
123			WHERE id = $1 AND state IN ('queued', 'sending') RETURNING attempts, first_attempt_at`, id, now).Scan(&attempts, &first)
124		if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
125			return 0, time.Time{}, false, nil
126		}
127		return attempts, first, err == nil, err
128	}
129	
130	// MarkSent records the provider's id.
131	func MarkSent(ctx context.Context, db DB, id, providerID string, at time.Time) (bool, error) {
132		return applied(db.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE messages SET state = 'sent', provider_message_id = $2, sent_at = $3, updated_at = now()
133			WHERE id = $1 AND state = 'sending'`, id, providerID, at))
134	}
135	
136	// MarkRetry puts a message back in the queue until next.
137	func MarkRetry(ctx context.Context, db DB, id, class, lastError string, next time.Time) (bool, error) {
138		return applied(db.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE messages SET state = 'queued', last_error_class = $2, last_error = $3, next_attempt_at = $4, updated_at = now()
139			WHERE id = $1 AND state = 'sending'`, id, class, lastError, next))
140	}
141	
142	// MarkFinal ends a message as failed or dead.
143	func MarkFinal(ctx context.Context, db DB, id, state, class, lastError string) (bool, error) {
144		return applied(db.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE messages SET state = $2, last_error_class = $3, last_error = $4, next_attempt_at = NULL, updated_at = now()
145			WHERE id = $1 AND state = 'sending'`, id, state, class, lastError))
146	}
147	
148	// MessageStates are the counted states of the stats API. Retrying is
149	// queued with attempts above 0 and is not counted as queued.
150	var MessageStates = []string{"queued", "retrying", "sending", "sent", "failed", "dead", "skipped"}
151	
152	// DeliveryStats counts a campaign's messages per channel and state, with
153	// every state of both channels present.
154	func DeliveryStats(ctx context.Context, db DB, campaignID string) (map[string]map[string]int, error) {
155		out := map[string]map[string]int{}
156		for _, ch := range []string{"sms", "email"} {
157			out[ch] = map[string]int{}
158			for _, s := range MessageStates {
159				out[ch][s] = 0
160			}
161		}
162		rows, err := db.Query(ctx, `SELECT channel::text,
163				CASE WHEN state = 'queued' AND attempts > 0 THEN 'retrying' ELSE state::text END, count(*)
164			FROM messages WHERE campaign_id = $1 GROUP BY 1, 2`, campaignID)
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, err
167		}
168		defer rows.Close()
169		for rows.Next() {
170			var ch, state string
171			var n int
172			if err := rows.Scan(&ch, &state, &n); err != nil {
173				return nil, err
174			}
175			out[ch][state] = n
176		}
177		return out, rows.Err()
178	}
179	
180	// Attention thresholds (rule 6). Sending for longer than twice the provider
181	// timeout means the worker probably died.
182	const (
183		StuckSendingAfter = 10 * time.Second
184		OverdueAfter      = 30 * time.Second
185		ManyAttempts      = 3
186	)
187	
188	// AttentionItem is a stuck or failed message, without contact data.
189	type AttentionItem struct {
190		ID             string     `json:"id"`
191		Channel        string     `json:"channel"`
192		State          string     `json:"state"`
193		Attempts       int        `json:"attempts"`
194		Reason         string     `json:"reason"` // stuck_sending, overdue, many_attempts, failed, dead
195		LastErrorClass *string    `json:"last_error_class"`
196		LastError      *string    `json:"last_error"`
197		NextAttemptAt  *time.Time `json:"next_attempt_at"`
198		UpdatedAt      time.Time  `json:"updated_at"`
199	}
200	
201	// Attention lists a campaign's messages that need a look, as of now.
202	func Attention(ctx context.Context, db DB, campaignID string, now time.Time) ([]AttentionItem, error) {
203		rows, err := db.Query(ctx, `SELECT id::text, channel::text, state::text, attempts,
204				CASE
205					WHEN state = 'sending' THEN 'stuck_sending'
206					WHEN state = 'queued' AND next_attempt_at < $2::timestamptz - $3::interval THEN 'overdue'
207					WHEN state = 'queued' THEN 'many_attempts'
208					ELSE state::text
209				END,
210				last_error_class::text, last_error, next_attempt_at, updated_at
211			FROM messages
212			WHERE campaign_id = $1 AND (
213				(state = 'sending' AND updated_at < $2::timestamptz - $4::interval)
214				OR (state = 'queued' AND (attempts >= $5 OR next_attempt_at < $2::timestamptz - $3::interval))
215				OR state IN ('failed', 'dead'))
216			ORDER BY updated_at, id`, campaignID, now, OverdueAfter, StuckSendingAfter, ManyAttempts)
217		if err != nil {
218			return nil, err
219		}
220		return pgx.CollectRows(rows, func(r pgx.CollectableRow) (AttentionItem, error) {
221			var a AttentionItem
222			err := r.Scan(&a.ID, &a.Channel, &a.State, &a.Attempts, &a.Reason, &a.LastErrorClass, &a.LastError, &a.NextAttemptAt, &a.UpdatedAt)
223			return a, err
224		})
225	}

72			Backoff:         delivery.RandomBackoff(rand.New(rand.NewPCG(rand.Uint64(), rand.Uint64()))),
73			Client:          &http.Client{},
74			Log:             log,
75		}
76		workers := river.NewWorkers()
77		river.AddWorker(workers, campaign.NewGenerateWorker(gen))
78		river.AddWorker(workers, fanout)
79		river.AddWorker(workers, send)
80		rc, err := river.NewClient(riverpgxv5.New(pool), jobs.ClientConfig(workers, log))
81		if err != nil {
82			return err
83		}
84		fanout.Jobs = rc
85		if err := rc.Start(ctx); err != nil {
86			return err
87		}
88		// Never log the key; only whether it is there.
89		log.Info("worker started", "llm_mode", getenv("LLM_MODE"), "model", client.Model(), "anthropic_key", keyState(getenv("LLM_MODE")))
90		<-ctx.Done()
91		stop, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
92		defer cancel()
93		return rc.Stop(stop)
94	}

96	func keyState(mode string) string {
97		if mode == "anthropic" {
98			return "present" // ConfigFromEnv refused to start without one
99		}
100		return "not used"
101	}
102	
103	// sleep waits for d or until ctx ends.
104	func sleep(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error {
105		t := time.NewTimer(d)
106		defer t.Stop()
107		select {
108		case <-ctx.Done():
109			return ctx.Err()
110		case <-t.C:
111			return nil
112		}
113	}
114	
115	// mockllmCmd serves the fake Messages API for LLM_MODE=mock. It needs no
116	// database and no key.
117	func mockllmCmd(ctx context.Context, log *slog.Logger, getenv func(string) string) error {
118		addr := getenv("MOCKLLM_ADDR")
119		if addr == "" {
120			addr = ":8090"
121		}
122		hs := &http.Server{Addr: addr, Handler: mockllmHandler(getenv), ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second}
123		return serve(ctx, log, hs, "mockllm listening")
124	}
125	
126	func mockllmHandler(getenv func(string) string) *mockllm.Server {
127		return mockllm.New(mockllm.Options{InvalidFirst: getenv("MOCKLLM_INVALID_FIRST") == "true"})
128	}
129	
130	// serve runs hs until ctx ends, then shuts it down.
131	func serve(ctx context.Context, log *slog.Logger, hs *http.Server, msg string) error {
132		go func() {
133			<-ctx.Done()
134			shutdown, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
135			defer cancel()
136			_ = hs.Shutdown(shutdown)
137		}()
138		log.Info(msg, "addr", hs.Addr)
139		if err := hs.ListenAndServe(); !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
140			return err
141		}
142		return nil
143	}

1	// Package jobs holds the River job argument types, queue names and worker
2	// settings. It is the contract between the side that inserts jobs (api,
3	// fan-out) and the workers, so both can be built in parallel. Kinds and
4	// queue names are stored in river_job rows: never rename one.
5	package jobs
6	
7	import (
8		"log/slog"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/riverqueue/river"
12	)
13	
14	// Queue names.
15	const (
16		QueueGenerate = "generate"
17		QueueFanout   = "fanout"
18		QueueSMS      = "sms"
19		QueueEmail    = "email"
20	)
21	
22	// QueueWorkers is how many jobs each queue runs at once in one worker process.
23	var QueueWorkers = map[string]int{
24		QueueGenerate: 2,
25		QueueFanout:   1,
26		QueueSMS:      20,
27		QueueEmail:    20,
28	}
29	
30	// Per-worker job timeouts.
31	const (
32		GenerateTimeout = 6 * time.Minute
33		SendTimeout     = 30 * time.Second
34	)
35	
36	// RescueStuckJobsAfter must exceed every job timeout. Otherwise the rescuer
37	// starts a second copy of a job that is still running.
38	const RescueStuckJobsAfter = 10 * time.Minute
39	
40	// GenerateArgs asks for one generation of a campaign at a given version. A
41	// job whose version no longer matches the campaign does nothing.
42	type GenerateArgs struct {
43		CampaignID string `json:"campaign_id"`
44		Version    int    `json:"version"`
45	}
46	
47	func (GenerateArgs) Kind() string { return "generate" }
48	
49	func (GenerateArgs) InsertOpts() river.InsertOpts {
50		return river.InsertOpts{Queue: QueueGenerate, UniqueOpts: river.UniqueOpts{ByArgs: true}}
51	}
52	
53	// FanoutArgs creates the messages and send jobs of an approved campaign.
54	type FanoutArgs struct {
55		CampaignID string `json:"campaign_id"`
56	}
57	
58	func (FanoutArgs) Kind() string { return "fanout" }
59	
60	func (FanoutArgs) InsertOpts() river.InsertOpts {
61		return river.InsertOpts{Queue: QueueFanout, UniqueOpts: river.UniqueOpts{ByArgs: true}}
62	}
63	
64	// SendArgs sends one message. It has no default queue: the inserter sets
65	// Queue to the message's channel (QueueSMS or QueueEmail), so each channel
66	// has its own workers.
67	type SendArgs struct {
68		MessageID string `json:"message_id"`
69	}
70	
71	func (SendArgs) Kind() string { return "send" }
72	
73	func (SendArgs) InsertOpts() river.InsertOpts {
74		return river.InsertOpts{UniqueOpts: river.UniqueOpts{ByArgs: true}}
75	}
76	
77	// ClientConfig is the River configuration of a worker process: every queue
78	// with its worker count, and the stuck-job rescue delay. Job timeouts are
79	// set per worker (GenerateTimeout, SendTimeout). An insert-only client (the
80	// api) needs no config beyond a driver.
81	func ClientConfig(workers *river.Workers, log *slog.Logger) *river.Config {
82		queues := make(map[string]river.QueueConfig, len(QueueWorkers))
83		for q, n := range QueueWorkers {
84			queues[q] = river.QueueConfig{MaxWorkers: n}
85		}
86		return &river.Config{
87			Queues:               queues,
88			Workers:              workers,
89			RescueStuckJobsAfter: RescueStuckJobsAfter,
90			Logger:               log,
91		}
92	}
93

1	// Package delivery sends approved campaigns: the fan-out job that creates
2	// messages and send jobs, the send workers, the per-channel rate limiter
3	// and the provider client.
4	package delivery
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8	
9		"golang.org/x/time/rate"
10	)
11	
12	// Rule 8: 100 messages per second per channel. Every provider call takes a
13	// token, retries included. With burst 1, no 1 s window holds more than 100
14	// calls; a burst of 100 could let close to 200 through.
15	const (
16		RatePerSecond = 100
17		Burst         = 1
18	)
19	
20	// Channels are the delivery channels, which are also the send queue names.
21	var Channels = []string{"sms", "email"}
22	
23	// NewLimiter returns one channel's limiter.
24	func NewLimiter() *rate.Limiter { return rate.NewLimiter(RatePerSecond, Burst) }
25	
26	// Limiter hands out one token per provider call. *rate.Limiter satisfies
27	// it.
28	type Limiter interface {
29		Wait(ctx context.Context) error
30	}
31	
32	// NewLimiters returns a limiter per channel, so a busy SMS queue never slows
33	// email.
34	func NewLimiters() map[string]Limiter {
35		out := make(map[string]Limiter, len(Channels))
36		for _, ch := range Channels {
37			out[ch] = NewLimiter()
38		}
39		return out
40	}

content.text:
The review holds up: ten of the eleven findings match the code, and F5 is only partly checkable from here. I verified by reading the cited code paths, not by re-running the reviewer's probes, and changed nothing.

Several "high" ratings are overstated for this project; the "Real impact" column gives my read.

| # | Claim | Verdict | Real impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Consent revoked during the limiter wait still sends | True | Low to medium. Consent is read in `LoadSend`, then `lim.Wait`, then `ClaimMessage` with no re-check ([send.go:90-102](internal/delivery/send.go:90)). The window is the limiter wait, bounded by the 30 s job timeout. |
| F2 | Failed completion check leaves the campaign `sending` | True | Medium. After `MarkSent`, a failed `CompleteIfDone` returns an error; the retry hits the terminal early return at [send.go:84](internal/delivery/send.go:84) and never re-checks. A later message finishing heals it, so it only sticks on the last message(s). No reconciler exists. |
| F3 | `evil.top`, `evil.click`, `evil.zip` pass validation | True | Medium. `domainRe` uses a fixed TLD list and `domainPathRe` needs a `/` ([validate.go:40-44](internal/content/validate.go:40)). The tests only cover `evil.top/login`. Phones do auto-link such bare domains, so this is a real gap in rule 4. |
| F4 | Exhausted generate job leaves the campaign `generating` | True, but narrow | Low. Nothing handles a discarded job. But River's default is 25 attempts, so it needs a very long outage; the probe forced one attempt. `generating -> cancelled` is allowed, so a human can get out. |
| F5 | Toolchain has known advisories | Partly verified | Local Go is 1.26.2 and `golang:1.26-alpine` floats, both confirmed. I could not confirm the 26 advisories or the "1.26.10" target: `govulncheck` is not installed. A fresh image build pulls the latest 1.26 patch anyway. |
| F6 | Retry re-renders the payload, provider answers 422 | True | Low here. `LoadSend` re-reads the user row each attempt and the mock provider returns 422 for the same key with another payload. It needs a recipient edit between a lost response and the retry, and nothing in this app edits users. |
| F7 | Body read error overrides a 4xx status | True | Low. The body is read before `Classify` ([send.go:225-230](internal/delivery/send.go:225)), so a 400 with a broken body becomes retryable `conn_reset`. Bounded by the 6-attempt cap. |
| F8 | Shutdown does not wait for in-flight requests | True | Medium. `ListenAndServe` returns as soon as `Shutdown` is called, and both `apiCmd` and `serve` return without waiting for it ([main.go:122](cmd/app/main.go:122), [worker.go:131](cmd/app/worker.go:131)). The 10 s drain is not honoured. |
| F9 | SSE has no write deadline | True | Low. The deadline is cleared once and never set again ([events.go:151](internal/httpapi/events.go:151)). A stalled reader can pin a handler, but the endpoint is behind the bearer token. |
| F10 | Rate limit is per process | True, already documented | Not a new finding. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:209` states that more worker replicas need a shared limiter, and compose runs one worker. |
| F11 | Never-attempted queued messages are not in "attention" | True | Low to medium. With `attempts = 0` and `next_attempt_at` NULL, the query at [delivery.go:214](internal/store/delivery.go:214) excludes them at any age. They do still show in the stats as `queued`. |

F1, F2, F7 and F8 are small fixes with obvious regression tests. F3 needs a decision from you first: catching any `label.label` shape will also flag text like a missing space after a full stop ("bitti.Hemen"), which is presumably why the path rule was chosen in commit `afda701`.

To settle F5, `govulncheck` would need installing; I have not checked it on pkg.go.dev yet, so say if you want that.

	DATABASE_URL='$(TEMPLATE_URL)' go run ./cmd/app migrate; \
	DATABASE_URL='$(TEMPLATE_URL)' go run ./cmd/app seed -as-of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z -seed 42 -users 5000; \
	env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY TEST_DATABASE_URL='$(TEST_PG)/postgres?sslmode=disable' REQUIRE_DB=1 go test -count=1 ./...; \
	$(MAKE) -s test-hooks

test-unit:
	env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY go test ./...

content.text:
All six findings are fixed, each with a regression test. `make lint` and `make test` pass, and nothing is committed.

**F1: consent revoked while the worker waits for a rate-limit token.** Claiming the message is now the cutoff for sending. `ClaimMessage` ([store/delivery.go](internal/store/delivery.go)) only claims a message if the recipient still has consent on that channel and the campaign is not cancelled. If the claim does not apply, the worker re-reads the message and skips it. Tests: consent revoked during the wait, and campaign cancelled during the wait. In both, the provider gets no call.

**F2: campaign left `sending` after a failed completion check.** When a job is retried and finds its message already finished, it now runs the completion check again instead of returning straight away. The test makes the first completion check fail, then confirms the retry completes the campaign without a second provider call.

**F7: a broken body turned a 400 into a retry.** The HTTP status is now classified before the body is read. A test covers 400, 422, 503 and 200, each with a broken body. A 200 with a broken body is still retried, because the provider may have sent it.

**F8: shutdown did not wait for active requests.** There is now one shared `serve`/`serveOn` in [worker.go](cmd/app/worker.go), used by the API and both mock servers. It returns only after active requests finish. If they take longer than 10 s, it logs a warning and closes the remaining connections. Tests cover both cases.

**F11: queued messages never attempted were not flagged.** A message still queued with zero attempts 2 minutes after fan-out now shows in "attention" as `not_started`. I picked 2 minutes: at 100 messages/s that is 12,000 messages per channel, more than the whole seed. Change it if you prefer another value. I added the reason to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` too. A worker heartbeat or backlog monitor is not part of this fix.

**F5: Go toolchain with known advisories.** I pinned Go 1.26.10, the latest 1.26 patch, in `go.mod` (`toolchain go1.26.10`) and in the Dockerfile (`golang:1.26.10-alpine`). [toolchain_test.go](cmd/app/toolchain_test.go) checks that the two pins match and fails if tests run on an older compiler; I confirmed it fails on your local 1.26.2.
- Two things were downloaded from the official Go servers: the 1.26.10 toolchain, which `go` fetched on its own because of the new line, and `govulncheck` v1.9.0, run once with `go run` and not added to `go.mod` or `go.sum`.
- govulncheck confirms the reviewer's count: 26 reachable advisories on 1.26.2, none on 1.26.10.

**Things to know:**
- **Dashboards and shutdown:** an open dashboard event stream (SSE) does not end on shutdown by itself, so with a dashboard open, shutdown waits the full 10 s and then cuts it. That is cleaner than before, but making the stream end on shutdown would be a small follow-up.
- **Tests on the old code:** I did not run the new F1 and F2 tests against the old code to watch them fail. The old code clearly fails them: it checked consent only before the wait, and returned early on a finished message.
- **Your uncommitted files:** `Dockerfile` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` already had your changes. I changed only the base-image line in one and two lines in the other.

Suggested commit message:

```
Fix review findings F1, F2, F5, F7, F8, F11

- delivery: the claim re-checks consent and cancellation after the rate
  limit wait, so it is the dispatch cutoff (F1)
- delivery: a run on a terminal message runs the completion check again,
  so a failed check no longer leaves the campaign sending (F2)
- delivery: classify the provider status before reading the body (F7)
- cmd/app: one serve helper that waits for active requests, with a
  bounded drain, for the api and both mocks (F8)
- store: never-attempted queued messages older than 2 minutes show as
  not_started in attention (F11)
- pin Go 1.26.10 in go.mod and the Dockerfile, with a test that keeps
  them equal; govulncheck clean (F5)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

### CI and dependency updates

Add GitHub Actions CI and Dependabot to this Go project. Before writing
anything, read `go.mod`, the package layout, any Dockerfile, and the
existing tests, so the workflow matches what the repo really contains.

**Workflow: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`**

Trigger on push to `main` and on every pull request. Set
`timeout-minutes` on every job so a hung connection cannot stall a run.

1. **lint-test** job:
   - `actions/setup-go` with `go-version-file: go.mod` and
     `cache-dependency-path: go.sum`.
   - `go vet ./...`
   - gofmt check: run `gofmt -l .` and fail if it prints anything,
     listing the offending files.
   - `staticcheck` (or `golangci-lint` if the repo already has a config).
   - `go test -race -count=3 -timeout 5m ./...` — `-race` because the
     code is concurrent network code; `-count=3` to surface flaky
     timing-dependent tests.
   - `govulncheck ./...` — blocking. If it fails on existing deps,
     report it to me rather than making it `continue-on-error`.
2. **fuzz** job, only if the repo decodes bytes off the wire (protocol
   frames, headers, custom encodings): add a `FuzzXxx` test for each
   parser and run each in CI with `-fuzztime=30s`.
3. **integration** job, only if some tests need real external services:
   gate them behind `//go:build integration`, provide the services with
   `services:` containers, and keep them out of the lint-test job.
4. **docker** job, only if a Dockerfile exists: build with
   `docker/build-push-action` (`push: false`, `load: true`, GHA cache),
   then smoke-test it: start the container, wait for its port, and hit a
   health or known endpoint. Exit code alone is not enough for a server.
5. **secrets** job: `gitleaks/gitleaks-action` with `fetch-depth: 0` so
   the whole history is scanned.

**Test hygiene the workflow relies on**

- Unit tests must be hermetic: no real internet. Use `httptest.NewServer`,
  `net.Pipe`, or listeners on `127.0.0.1:0`.
- Tests that depend on a fixture or service fail with `t.Fatalf` when it
  is missing; they never silently `t.Skip`.
- If practical, add `go.uber.org/goleak` in `TestMain` to catch leaked
  connection-handler goroutines.

**Dependabot: `.github/dependabot.yml`**

`version: 2`, with weekly updates for:
- `gomod` at `/`
- `github-actions` at `/`
- `docker` at `/` — only if a Dockerfile exists

Group minor and patch updates into one PR per ecosystem to cut noise, and
set `open-pull-requests-limit: 5`.

**Done when**

- The workflow passes on a clean checkout, and you show me the run or
  the local equivalent of each step.
- Any test you had to fix, mark, or gate (for flakiness, network
  access, or a missing fixture) is listed with the reason.
- A CI status badge is added to the top of the README.
- Nothing is committed unless I ask.

content.content:
## 3. Components

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  UI["Vue 3 SPA (Vite, TS)"] -->|REST + SSE| API["api (Go)"]
  API -->|enqueue, LISTEN| PG[("Postgres: app tables + River jobs")]
  W["worker (Go, River)"] --> PG
  W -->|Messages API| Claude["Claude API, or mockllm in mock mode"]
  W -->|HTTP + Idempotency-Key| MP["mockprovider (Go)"]
  MP --> MPDB[("Postgres: mockprovider db")]
  OPS["/healthz /readyz"] -.- API
```

- **api**: HTTP handlers, validation, state machine, SSE streams. It holds an insert-only River client: generate, approve and cancel touch their jobs in the same transaction as their transition. It never calls Claude and never needs the key.
- **worker**: River client. Runs the generate job (both LLM stages), the fan-out job and the per-channel send jobs, with the rate limiter and the retry policy. It is the only service that calls Claude and the provider, so it is the only container that may receive `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- **mockllm**: an HTTP fake of the Messages API (section 5). The worker uses it through the real SDK when `LLM_MODE=mock`, the compose default.
- **mockprovider**: one message endpoint with fault injection and idempotency storage (section 8).
- **Postgres**: one server. App tables and River tables in the `app` database, provider state in a separate `mockprovider` database with its own role, which cannot connect to `app` (`deploy/postgres-init`). So the mock cannot cheat by reading app tables.
- `api`, `worker`, `mockllm`, `mockprovider`, `migrate` and `seed` are subcommands of one binary (`cmd/app`). `docker compose up` runs migrations, seeds about 5,000 users and starts everything.

## 5. LLM integration (rules 4, 5)

Generation is a River job (`generate`, `internal/campaign`) that the worker runs. `POST /api/campaigns/{id}/generate` moves the campaign to `generating`, writes a `started` event and enqueues the job in one transaction, then answers 202 with the URL of this generation's event stream. The job does nothing unless the campaign is still `generating` at the job's version, and it checks that again, under a row lock, before every write. So a cancel or a newer generation always wins.

Two calls per generation, matching the user flow in the spec:

1. **Segment stage** (streamed, nothing shown live): brief + field catalog → the segment rule itself (`schemas/segment_rule.schema.json`). The backend validates it, counts the audience and writes a `segment_ready` event with the rule, the counts and a description that our code generates from the rule (`segment.Describe`). So the marketer reviews what will actually run, not the model's claim about it.
2. **Content stage** (streamed live): brief + our segment description + allowed variables + limits → `{sms: {body}, email: {subject, body}}`. The model writes plain text only, with no links: any URL or email address fails validation, and links come only from the `{{campaign_url}}` variable, which the backend fills from campaign config. HTML email is produced by our own `html/template` from that text, so model output is never raw HTML.

**Client** (`internal/llm`): `anthropic-sdk-go/v2`, model `claude-opus-5-5` (env `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`), adaptive thinking, effort set explicitly (`low` for the segment, `medium` for content), JSON outputs (`output_config.format`) with the API-derived schema. Server-side refusal fallback (`fallbacks: "default"`, beta header `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01`, set with `option.WithJSONSet` since there is no typed field) is enabled; a final refusal is still a loud failure. SDK retries are off (`option.WithMaxRetries(0)`), so all retries go through our own policy (section 7). The SDK's environment defaults are skipped (`WithoutEnvironmentDefaults`), so only the client's config decides the base URL and the credential, and the key goes in `x-api-key` (`WithAPIKey` in v2.8.0 sends a bearer token). `LLM_MODE=mock` points the client at mockllm and never reads the key; `LLM_MODE=anthropic` without a key stops the worker at start.

**Validation pipeline** (same code for LLM output and human edits):

1. `stop_reason` check: `refusal` fails with no retry. `max_tokens` counts as invalid and is retried.
2. Parse JSON, then validate against the **full** schema with `santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` (draft 2020-12).
3. Semantic checks: DSL fields, operators and value types; variable allowlist; rendered length limits (section 6); link policy.
4. On failure: append the failed answer unchanged (thinking blocks included, since preserved thinking forbids editing earlier turns), then a user turn with the errors as JSON, and retry: max 3 validation attempts per stage. Transport failures (section 7) are retried separately, up to 3 times per attempt with `retry.Backoff`, and never use up a validation attempt; 400 and 401 are never retried. Every call writes an `llm_calls` row (outcome, error class, raw output, tokens, latency, `prompt_version`), each failed attempt is logged and pushed as an `attempt_failed` event, and after the third failure the campaign moves to `generation_failed` with a `failed` event that carries the errors. Nothing is truncated or defaulted to make output fit.

**Two schemas, one source**: the structured-outputs API does not support `maxLength`, `minimum`/`maximum` or recursion. So `schemas/*.json` holds the full schema, and the API schema is derived from it by stripping unsupported keywords. A test asserts the derived schema contains no unsupported keyword, and that a sample payload valid against the full schema is also valid against the derived one. Because recursion is unsupported, the DSL has a fixed depth.

**Event log and streaming**: every step of a generation is a row in `generation_events`, written with `pg_notify` in the same transaction:

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `started` | the generation's version (written by `POST /generate`) |
| `segment_ready` | rule, description, counts |
| `delta` | stage, attempt, field (`sms.body`, `email.subject`, `email.body`), the new text |
| `attempt_failed` | stage, attempt, errors (or the transport class, when streamed copy must be cleared) |
| `done` | revision id |
| `failed` | reason (`invalid_output`, `refusal`, `transport_error`, `cancelled`), stage, errors |

The worker runs a small partial-JSON extractor over the content stream and writes `delta` events, merged per field every 150 ms. `GET /api/campaigns/{id}/events` is SSE: the backlog after `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after=`, for curl), then live events, a heartbeat comment every 15 s, and the end after `done` or `failed`. The event id is the row id. One LISTEN connection per api process feeds an in-memory hub, so streams do not hold a database connection each, and a 1 s poll covers a missed notification. The handler clears its write deadline, so the server's `WriteTimeout` does not cut the stream. The token travels only in the `Authorization` header, so the browser reads the stream with `fetch`: `EventSource` cannot send that header. The UI shows deltas as provisional until `done`, and clears them on `attempt_failed`.

**Cancel during generation**: `POST /cancel` moves the campaign to `cancelled`, writes `failed` with reason `cancelled`, and cancels the generate job with River's `JobCancelTx`, all in one transaction. A running job has its context cancelled; the job then stops without writing anything more.

**Testability**: `internal/mockllm` is an HTTP fake of `POST /v1/messages` that speaks the real SSE event sequence and answers 400 to request shapes the real API rejects (unsupported schema keywords, `temperature`, forced `tool_choice`, non-adaptive thinking). Tests run the real client and SDK against it with `option.WithBaseURL`, scripting replies (invalid then valid, refusal, `max_tokens`, 529, 429 with `Retry-After`, a stall, hostile outputs) and reading the recorded requests. Without a script, a small demo brain answers from brief keywords, which is what compose runs in mock mode. `make test` also unsets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` so no test can reach the real API by accident.

## 9. Live status and monitoring

- **Delivery stats**: `GET /api/campaigns/{id}/stats` counts messages per channel and state (`queued`, `retrying` = queued with attempts above 0, `sending`, `sent`, `failed`, `dead`, `skipped`), every state present for both channels. A live delivery stream for the dashboard is not built yet; when it is, it reads with `fetch` like the generation stream, since `EventSource` cannot send the token.
- **Metrics** (planned, not built yet: `/metrics`, `prometheus/client_golang`), with low-cardinality labels and no campaign or user ids:
  - `messages_total{channel,outcome}`
  - `provider_requests_total{channel,class}`
  - `provider_request_duration_seconds{channel}`
  - `retries_total{channel,reason}`
  - `queue_jobs{queue,state}`
  - `rate_limiter_wait_seconds{channel}`
  - `llm_requests_total{stage,outcome}`
  - `llm_validation_failures_total{stage,rule}`
  - `worker_last_processed_timestamp_seconds`
- **Health**: `/healthz` is liveness only (the process is up, no dependency checks, per Kubernetes guidance). `/readyz` checks the DB ping, applied migrations and the River client.
- **Logs**: `slog` JSON with request id and message id. No phone numbers or email addresses in logs, and never the key: startup logs only `anthropic_key=present`.

| Table | Key columns |

## 5. LLM integration (rules 4, 5)

Generation is a River job (`generate`, `internal/campaign`) that the worker runs. `POST /api/campaigns/{id}/generate` moves the campaign to `generating`, writes a `started` event and enqueues the job in one transaction, then answers 202 with the URL of this generation's event stream. The job does nothing unless the campaign is still `generating` at the job's version, and it checks that again, under a row lock, before every write. So a cancel or a newer generation always wins.

Two calls per generation, matching the user flow in the spec:

1. **Segment stage** (streamed, nothing shown live): brief + field catalog → the segment rule itself (`schemas/segment_rule.schema.json`). The backend validates it, counts the audience and writes a `segment_ready` event with the rule, the counts and a description that our code generates from the rule (`segment.Describe`). So the marketer reviews what will actually run, not the model's claim about it.
2. **Content stage** (streamed live): brief + our segment description + allowed variables + limits → `{sms: {body}, email: {subject, body}}`. The model writes plain text only, with no links: any URL or email address fails validation, and links come only from the `{{campaign_url}}` variable, which the backend fills from campaign config. HTML email is produced by our own `html/template` from that text, so model output is never raw HTML.

**Client** (`internal/llm`): `anthropic-sdk-go/v2`, model `claude-opus-5-5` (env `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`), adaptive thinking, effort set explicitly (`low` for the segment, `medium` for content), JSON outputs (`output_config.format`) with the API-derived schema. Server-side refusal fallback (`fallbacks: "default"`, beta header `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01`, set with `option.WithJSONSet` since there is no typed field) is enabled; a final refusal is still a loud failure. SDK retries are off (`option.WithMaxRetries(0)`), so all retries go through our own policy (section 7). The SDK's environment defaults are skipped (`WithoutEnvironmentDefaults`), so only the client's config decides the base URL and the credential, and the key goes in `x-api-key` (`WithAPIKey` in v2.8.0 sends a bearer token). `LLM_MODE=mock` points the client at mockllm and never reads the key; `LLM_MODE=anthropic` without a key stops the worker at start.

**Validation pipeline** (same code for LLM output and human edits):

1. `stop_reason` check: `refusal` fails with no retry. `max_tokens` counts as invalid and is retried.
2. Parse JSON, then validate against the **full** schema with `santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` (draft 2020-12).
3. Semantic checks: DSL fields, operators and value types; variable allowlist; rendered length limits (section 6); link policy.
4. On failure: append the failed answer unchanged (thinking blocks included, since preserved thinking forbids editing earlier turns), then a user turn with the errors as JSON, and retry: max 3 validation attempts per stage. Transport failures (section 7) are retried separately, up to 3 times per attempt with `retry.Backoff`, and never use up a validation attempt; 400 and 401 are never retried. Every call writes an `llm_calls` row (outcome, error class, raw output, tokens, latency, `prompt_version`), each failed attempt is logged and pushed as an `attempt_failed` event, and after the third failure the campaign moves to `generation_failed` with a `failed` event that carries the errors. Nothing is truncated or defaulted to make output fit.

**Two schemas, one source**: the structured-outputs API does not support `maxLength`, `minimum`/`maximum` or recursion. So `schemas/*.json` holds the full schema, and the API schema is derived from it by stripping unsupported keywords. A test asserts the derived schema contains no unsupported keyword, and that a sample payload valid against the full schema is also valid against the derived one. Because recursion is unsupported, the DSL has a fixed depth.

**Event log and streaming**: every step of a generation is a row in `generation_events`, written with `pg_notify` in the same transaction:

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `started` | the generation's version (written by `POST /generate`) |
| `segment_ready` | rule, description, counts |
| `delta` | stage, attempt, field (`sms.body`, `email.subject`, `email.body`), the new text |
| `attempt_failed` | stage, attempt, errors (or the transport class, when streamed copy must be cleared) |
| `done` | revision id |
| `failed` | reason (`invalid_output`, `refusal`, `transport_error`, `cancelled`), stage, errors |

The worker runs a small partial-JSON extractor over the content stream and writes `delta` events, merged per field every 150 ms. `GET /api/campaigns/{id}/events` is SSE: the backlog after `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after=`, for curl), then live events, a heartbeat comment every 15 s, and the end after `done` or `failed`. The event id is the row id. One LISTEN connection per api process feeds an in-memory hub, so streams do not hold a database connection each, and a 1 s poll covers a missed notification. The handler clears its write deadline, so the server's `WriteTimeout` does not cut the stream. The token travels only in the `Authorization` header, so the browser reads the stream with `fetch`: `EventSource` cannot send that header. The UI shows deltas as provisional until `done`, and clears them on `attempt_failed`.

**Cancel during generation**: `POST /cancel` moves the campaign to `cancelled`, writes `failed` with reason `cancelled`, and cancels the generate job with River's `JobCancelTx`, all in one transaction. A running job has its context cancelled; the job then stops without writing anything more.

**Testability**: `internal/mockllm` is an HTTP fake of `POST /v1/messages` that speaks the real SSE event sequence and answers 400 to request shapes the real API rejects (unsupported schema keywords, `temperature`, forced `tool_choice`, non-adaptive thinking). Tests run the real client and SDK against it with `option.WithBaseURL`, scripting replies (invalid then valid, refusal, `max_tokens`, 529, 429 with `Retry-After`, a stall, hostile outputs) and reading the recorded requests. Without a script, a small demo brain answers from brief keywords, which is what compose runs in mock mode. `make test` also unsets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` so no test can reach the real API by accident.

questions.question: What should the eval harness measure, and against which model? The real model needs the API key, so you would run that part yourself.

options.label: Golden briefs, both modes (Recommended)
options.description: A fixed set of about 20 briefs (normal, vague, Turkish, hostile/injection) with expected segment properties. `app eval` runs the real generate pipeline and reports: valid on first attempt, valid after repair, attempts, refusals, segment match against the expectation, latency, tokens. CI and I run it against mockllm; you run it once with LLM_MODE=anthropic and the numbers go in the README.

options.label: Mock only
options.description: Same harness, but numbers only from mockllm. No key ever needed, but the numbers say little about Claude.

options.label: Delivery numbers only
options.description: No LLM eval. Report pipeline numbers from the chaos run instead: throughput, retries, duplicates, time to drain.

questions.question: How should the Vue app be served?

options.label: Embedded in the api binary (Recommended)
options.description: A Node stage in the Dockerfile builds web/dist, and the api serves it with go:embed at /. Same origin, so no CORS and no extra container. `docker compose up` gives one URL. Vite dev server proxies /api in development.

options.label: Separate web container
options.description: nginx serves the build and proxies /api to the api. One more service and image, but the Go binary stays frontend-free.

questions.question: How should the delivery dashboard update live?

options.label: Poll every second (Recommended)
options.description: The UI polls the existing /stats and /messages?filter=attention while the campaign is sending. No new backend code, and at 100 msg/s a 1 s refresh looks live.

options.label: New SSE stream
options.description: A delivery stream endpoint pushing stats snapshots, read with fetch like the generation stream. More backend work and tests for a similar visible result.

questions.question: Your CI text asks for `//go:build integration` tags. The repo already gates DB tests with TEST_DATABASE_URL, and REQUIRE_DB=1 turns a skip into a failure. Which do you want?

options.label: Keep REQUIRE_DB (Recommended)
options.description: No build tags. lint-test runs unit tests with -race -count=3 (DB tests skip there). A separate integration job gets a Postgres service container, builds the template and runs with REQUIRE_DB=1, so a missing database fails loudly. No test files change.

options.label: Add build tags
options.description: Tag every *_db_test.go with //go:build integration, as the description says. Touches about 20 test files and the Makefile.

# Plan: Vue frontend, eval harness, metrics and health, CI

## Context

The backend is complete through delivery (stages A and B plus the review fixes). What is left from `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 15 is the user-facing part and the operational part:

- There is no `web/` directory yet. The marketer flow (brief, audience preview, streamed copy, edit, approve, live dashboard) only exists as an API.
- `/metrics` is planned but not built. `/readyz` does not check River yet. The worker exposes nothing.
- There are no numbers on how well generation works, and no CI.

Decisions already taken with the user:

- Eval: golden briefs, run in both modes. Mock mode in CI and by agents. Anthropic mode is run by the user only (rule 1).
- Frontend is served by a **separate web container** (nginx), not embedded in the Go binary.
- Dashboard is live by **polling every second**, no new SSE stream.
- CI keeps the existing `REQUIRE_DB` gating. No `//go:build integration` tags.

The four work streams below touch disjoint files, so they can run as parallel sessions (CLAUDE.md section 5). Order only matters at the end: CI is written last because it runs what the others add.

---

## Stream 1: Vue frontend (`web/`)

**Stack**: Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript, Vitest. Vue Router for two routes. No state library (one composable per concern) and no UI kit: plain CSS. Each npm dependency is checked (maintenance, license, exact version) and reported in chat before it is added, as CLAUDE.md asks for Go modules.

**Layout**

```
web/
  package.json, vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, index.html
  nginx.conf            serves dist, proxies /api, /healthz, /readyz to api:8080
  Dockerfile            node build stage -> nginx (unprivileged) stage
  src/
    api/client.ts       fetch wrapper: bearer header, {path, code, message} errors, 409 handling
    api/types.ts        Campaign, Revision, Event, Issue, Stats, AttentionItem (mirror the Go JSON)
    api/sse.ts          fetch-based SSE reader: parses id/event/data, resumes with Last-Event-ID
    stream/reducer.ts   pure reducer over generation events (see below)
    composables/useCampaign.ts, useGeneration.ts, usePolling.ts
    views/ComposeView.vue     brief form -> create -> generate
    views/CampaignView.vue    one page whose panel depends on campaign.state
    components/TokenGate.vue, SegmentCard.vue, CopyEditor.vue, IssueList.vue,
               ApproveBar.vue, DeliveryDashboard.vue, AttentionTable.vue, AuditTrail.vue
```

**Screens, mapped to the existing API** (`internal/httpapi`)

1. **Token gate**. Asks for the admin token once and keeps it in `sessionStorage`. The README names the dev token. The token is sent only in the `Authorization` header.
2. **Brief** (`POST /api/campaigns`, then `POST /{id}/generate` with `version`). Fields: brief, campaign URL. 422 issues render next to the field through `IssueList`.
3. **Generation** (`GET /{id}/events` read with `fetch`, since `EventSource` cannot send the header).
   - `segment_ready`: `SegmentCard` shows our `description`, the rule, and the counts (total, SMS eligible, email eligible). This is the audience preview.
   - `delta`: copy appears per field, marked provisional.
   - `attempt_failed`: provisional copy is cleared and the errors are listed ("attempt 1 of 3 failed").
   - `done`: reload the campaign and show the stored revision. `failed`: show reason and errors, offer Regenerate.
4. **Review and edit** (state `in_review`). `CopyEditor` edits SMS body, email subject and body. Save is `POST /{id}/revisions` with `base_revision_id`; 422 issues map to fields by `path` (`/sms/body`, ...). Warnings (SMS segments) show as non-blocking. The audience counts refresh from the new revision. Actions: Approve (`POST /approve` with `revision_id` and `version`), Reject, Regenerate, Cancel. A 409 reloads the campaign and tells the user it changed.
5. **Dashboard** (states `approved`, `sending`, `completed*`, `cancelled`). `usePolling` hits `/stats` and `/messages?filter=attention` every second while the campaign is `approved` or `sending`, then once more and stops. Per channel: a stacked bar and counts for queued, retrying, sending, sent, failed, dead, skipped. "Needs attention" table with reason (including the new `not_started`), attempts, last error class, next attempt. Audit trail from `campaign.events`.

**Stream reducer** (`stream/reducer.ts`, pure, the main Vitest target): state `{phase, segment, fields, attempt, errors, lastEventId}`. Rules: ignore events with id at or below `lastEventId` (replay after reconnect); `delta` appends to its field; `attempt_failed` clears fields; `done` and `failed` are terminal.

**Rules that apply to the UI**

- Rule 4 and 9: model text and API text render only through Vue interpolation. No `v-html` anywhere; a test greps `src/` for it. The UI shows no recipient contact data, and the API sends none.
- Rule 5: validation failures are shown, never hidden: attempt errors during generation, field errors on edit.

**Serving**

- `web/Dockerfile`: `node:22-alpine` build stage (`npm ci`, `npm run build`), then `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged` with `nginx.conf`. The `/api/` location sets `proxy_buffering off`, `proxy_http_version 1.1` and a long `proxy_read_timeout` so SSE passes through.
- `docker-compose.yml`: new `web` service, `127.0.0.1:8081:8080`, depends on `api`. Same origin through the proxy, so the api needs no CORS code.
- Dev: `vite.config.ts` proxies `/api` to `127.0.0.1:8080`.
- `Makefile`: `web-test` (`npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test`), called from `make test`.

**Tests (Vitest)**: reducer (order, replay, clear on failure, terminal states); SSE parser (chunks split mid-line, heartbeat comments, multi-line data); `IssueList` and field mapping of 422 bodies; polling stops on a terminal state; no `v-html`.

---

## Stream 2: Eval harness and numbers

**Goal**: numbers on how often generation produces valid, correct output, and at what cost.

**New**

- `evals/briefs.json`: about 20 cases. Each has `id`, `brief`, `category` (`plain`, `turkish`, `vague`, `multi_condition`, `injection`) and `expect`:
  - `segment`: properties the rule must have, such as `city=istanbul`, an event condition `cart_add` within N days, a negated `purchase`. Not exact JSON equality.
  - `audience`: optional `[min, max]` on the fixed seed.
  - `must_fail`: for briefs that should end in refusal or failure.
  - Injection cases assert the structural guarantees: no URL or email in copy, only allowlisted variables, consent still applied (eligible counts at or below total).
- `internal/eval/`: loads the cases, runs each through the real pipeline, scores it, aggregates.
  - It reuses `campaign.Generator.Run` (`internal/campaign/generate.go`) directly, with no River and no HTTP: insert a campaign in `generating`, run, then read `llm_calls`, `generation_events` and the revision through `internal/store`. So the eval measures the same code the worker runs.
  - Segment scoring walks the validated `segment.Rule`; audience comes from `segment.CountAudience`.
- `cmd/app/eval.go`: subcommand `app eval [-cases evals/briefs.json] [-out evals/results] [-runs N]`. It builds the LLM client with `llm.ConfigFromEnv`, so `LLM_MODE` decides the target, exactly like the worker.
- `make eval`: runs against the throwaway Postgres template and mockllm (in-process `httptest` server from `internal/mockllm`), no key.

**Metrics reported** (JSON plus a Markdown table):

| Metric | Source |
|---|---|
| valid on first attempt, valid after repair, failed (per stage) | `llm_calls.outcome`, `attempt` |
| mean attempts per stage, refusals, transport errors | `llm_calls` |
| segment match rate, audience-in-range rate | scorer |
| injection cases holding every structural check | scorer |
| latency p50 and p95, input and output tokens per generation | `llm_calls` |
| failure reasons by validation code | `llm_calls.validation_errors` |

**Who runs what** (rule 1)

- Agents and CI: `make eval` in mock mode only. This proves the harness; its numbers describe the demo brain, and the report says so in its header (`mode`, `model`, `prompt_version`).
- The user: `LLM_MODE=anthropic make eval` in their own terminal. The results file holds no key and no recipient data, so it is safe to hand back for the README table.

**Tests**: the scorer on hand-written rules (match, miss, negation); aggregation on fixed `llm_calls` rows; one end-to-end run of three cases against scripted mockllm replies (valid, invalid then valid, refusal) with exact expected numbers.

---

## Stream 3: Metrics and health

**Dependency**: `github.com/prometheus/client_golang` (already named in ARCHITECTURE section 13). Check pkg.go.dev for version and license and report before adding.

**New package `internal/metrics`**: one `Registry` struct that owns a private `prometheus.Registry` (no global default, so tests are isolated) and the collectors from ARCHITECTURE section 9, with the same names and labels:

`messages_total{channel,outcome}`, `provider_requests_total{channel,class}`, `provider_request_duration_seconds{channel}`, `retries_total{channel,reason}`, `rate_limiter_wait_seconds{channel}`, `llm_requests_total{stage,outcome}`, `llm_validation_failures_total{stage,rule}`, `worker_last_processed_timestamp_seconds`, `queue_jobs{queue,state}`.

Labels are closed sets only (channel, retry class, stage, validation code). No campaign, message or user id.

**Wiring** (small optional interfaces, nil means no-op, so existing tests keep passing unchanged):

- `internal/delivery/send.go`: `SendWorker.Metrics`. Observe limiter wait around `lim.Wait`, request duration and class in `post`, outcome at each terminal update, retry reason before `JobSnooze`, last-processed time at the end of `Work`.
- `internal/campaign/generate.go`: `Generator.Metrics`. Count each call outcome where `record` is called, and each validation issue code.
- `queue_jobs`: a collector that runs one `GROUP BY queue, state` query on `river_job` at scrape time, with a 2 s timeout (query added to `internal/store`).
- `cmd/app/worker.go`: the worker gets a small HTTP listener (`WORKER_METRICS_ADDR`, default `:9090`) with `/metrics` and `/healthz`, run through the existing `serveOn` helper. Compose publishes it on `127.0.0.1:9090`.
- `internal/httpapi/server.go`: `GET /metrics` outside auth (as section 11 states), with api-side metrics: `http_requests_total{route,status}` using the mux pattern as `route`, and `sse_streams` gauge.

**Health**

- `/healthz` stays liveness only.
- `/readyz` adds the River check that section 9 promises: the `river_job` table is queryable (migrations applied for River too).
- Worker `/healthz`: 200 while the River client is started and not stopping. This gives compose a healthcheck for the worker and closes the gap from review finding F11 (a dead worker is now visible outside the dashboard).
- `docker-compose.yml`: healthchecks for `api` (`/readyz`) and `worker`.

**Tests**: metric names and label sets are asserted against a golden list (a guard against high-cardinality labels); a send test asserts counter deltas for ok, 503 then ok, and 400; `/metrics` is reachable without a token and contains no id-shaped label; `/readyz` fails when the River table is missing; worker health flips on stop.

**Docs**: update ARCHITECTURE sections 9 and 11 from "planned" to built.

---

## Stream 4: CI and Dependabot

Follows the user's description, adapted to this repo. Written last.

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: on push to `main` and on pull requests. `timeout-minutes` on every job. `permissions: contents: read`.

1. **lint-test** (no database):
   - `actions/setup-go` with `go-version-file: go.mod` (picks the pinned `toolchain go1.26.10`) and `cache-dependency-path: go.sum`.
   - `go vet ./...`; gofmt check that lists offending files (same logic as `make lint`).
   - `staticcheck` at a pinned version. No golangci config exists, so staticcheck it is.
   - `go test -race -count=3 -timeout 5m ./...` with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset. DB tests skip here by design; the integration job is where they must run.
   - `govulncheck ./...` at v1.9.0, blocking. It is clean today on 1.26.10.
   - `make test-hooks` (the guard-secrets and pre-commit table tests).
2. **integration**: `services: postgres` (same image and settings as `postgres-test` in compose, port 55432). Steps mirror `make test` without docker compose: create `app_template`, `app migrate`, `app seed -as-of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z -seed 42 -users 5000`, then `REQUIRE_DB=1 TEST_DATABASE_URL=... go test -race -count=1 -timeout 10m ./...`. `REQUIRE_DB=1` makes a missing database a failure, never a skip (`internal/testdb`).
3. **fuzz**: the four existing targets, 30 s each: `FuzzExtractFieldsNeverPanics`, `FuzzExtractFieldsPrefix` (`internal/llm`), `FuzzCompileShape` (`internal/segment`), `FuzzParse` (`internal/content`). No new fuzz tests are needed: these are the parsers of untrusted bytes.
4. **web**: `actions/setup-node` with npm cache; `npm ci`, typecheck, `npm test`, `npm run build`.
5. **eval**: `make eval`-equivalent in mock mode against the same Postgres service; uploads the report as an artifact. Proves the harness runs; no key in CI.
6. **docker**: `docker/build-push-action` (`push: false`, `load: true`, GHA cache) for the app image and the web image. Smoke test: `docker compose up -d --wait`, then curl `/healthz`, `/readyz`, an authenticated `POST /api/audience/count` with the dev token, the web root, and the worker `/metrics`. Compose runs in the default mock mode.
7. **secrets**: `gitleaks/gitleaks-action` with `fetch-depth: 0`.

All third-party actions are pinned to a commit SHA with the version in a comment.

**Test hygiene**

- Hermetic already: tests use `httptest`, mockllm and mockprovider. Confirm during the work by running the unit job with network off locally, and list anything that breaks.
- `goleak` in `TestMain`: try it in `internal/delivery` and `internal/httpapi` only. If pgx or River background goroutines make it noisy, drop it and report why, instead of adding a long ignore list. It is a new test dependency, so check and report it first.
- Any test that proves flaky under `-race -count=3` is fixed or reported, never silently skipped.

**`.github/dependabot.yml`**: `version: 2`, weekly, `open-pull-requests-limit: 5`, minor and patch grouped per ecosystem, for `gomod` at `/`, `github-actions` at `/`, `docker` at `/` and `/web`, `npm` at `/web`. Note for the user: the `toolchain` line and the Dockerfile tag must move together (`TestToolchainPinned` enforces it), so a Dependabot Docker bump of the Go image will fail CI until `go.mod` is bumped too. That is intended.

**README**: there is no README yet. Create a minimal one now (title, CI badge, quick start with `make up`, the dev token, URLs, how to run tests and the eval). The full README stays build-order step 7.

---

## Order and parallelism

| Step | Stream | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| A | 1 Frontend, 2 Eval, 3 Metrics and health | nothing; parallel, disjoint files |
| B | Compose and Makefile edits (web service, healthchecks, `make eval`, `make web-test`) | A; one session, since all three touch these two files |
| C | 4 CI, Dependabot, README stub | A and B |

Shared files, edited only in step B or C to avoid conflicts: `docker-compose.yml`, `Makefile`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `cmd/app/main.go` (new `eval` subcommand: one `case` line).

`DECISIONS.md` is not touched. New decisions (nginx container, polling, eval scope, goleak outcome, each new dependency) are reported in chat for the user to record. Nothing is committed; a commit message is suggested per stream.

## Verification

- `make lint` and `make test` green, with no API key, after each stream.
- **Frontend**: `npm test` green. Then `make up` and walk the flow in the browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8081`: token, brief, watch the segment card and streamed copy, set `MOCKLLM_INVALID_FIRST=true` once to see the attempt error and clear, make an invalid edit (a URL in the SMS) and see the field error, approve, watch the dashboard drain to completed, and see failed or dead rows in "Needs attention" under the mock provider's chaos settings.
- **Eval**: `make eval` prints the table and writes `evals/results/`. The scripted three-case test gives exact numbers. The user runs anthropic mode and shares the report.
- **Metrics**: `curl 127.0.0.1:8080/metrics` and `127.0.0.1:9090/metrics` during a send; counters move and `messages_total` sums to the dashboard totals. Stop the worker: its healthcheck fails and `not_started` rows appear after 2 minutes.
- **CI**: run the local equivalent of every job step and show the output (vet, gofmt, staticcheck, race x3, govulncheck, fuzz 30 s each, integration against `postgres-test`, web build, docker build plus smoke). The real run is checked after the user pushes.
